title: Fuzzy SLO Gatekeeper: absorbive backoff + atomic circuit debouncer (hotfix)
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: transient latency spikes and rapid regional circuit flips during a recent incident caused aggressive tenant evictions and cascading failovers. This PR introduces a "fuzzy" SLO gatekeeper that smooths short-lived latency excursions and a small atomic circuit debouncer to prevent rapid open/reopen cycles. Goals: 1) reduce unnecessary tenant evictions caused by noise, 2) ensure graceful regional failover decisions remain conservative during short spikes, 3) preserve observability for post-incident analysis. Summary of changes: added a sliding-median-based smoother in runtime/slo/gatekeeper.go that treats the SLO signal as a noisy measurement and computes a fuzzy pass/fail score rather than a binary threshold; introduced a tenant-level absorbive backoff state machine (tenant/state.go) that tracks consecutive transient violations and applies an exponentially increasing cooldown window before placing tenant in full eviction; added an atomic circuit debouncer layer in routing/circuit_manager.go to enforce a minimum stable window for circuit transitions and avoid quick flip-flops; wired telemetry: new metrics slo.fuzzy_score, slo.violation_streak, circuit.debounce_count and events for tenant.cooldown_start/complete; added unit and integration tests (runtime/slo/*, routing/*) plus a focused chaos test that simulates short spikes across multiple regions. Rollout plan: hotfix channel -> canary in us-west-2 (2 nodes) -> -wide ramp with a 1-hour verification window and automatic rollback on increased eviction rate. See linked Linear items for post-rollout observability dashboard tasks and a follow-up plan to tune median window length per workload.
